issue.title: run_shell_command always reports "Stderr: (empty)" and puts stderr output under "Stdout:"

steps: Run exactly python3 -c "import sys; print('to-stdout'); print('to-stderr', file=sys.stderr)" using run_shell_command. Tell me separately what was printed to stdout and stderr, quoting the tool result.
expected: Output labels accurately distinguish stdout and stderr, or state that the streams are combined.
defect: The model-facing tool result puts to-stderr under Stdout and hardcodes Stderr: (empty).

fault location.explanation: formatNormalOutput formats the merged filteredOutput under Stdout and always emits the literal Stderr: (empty). This contradicts the advertised separate-stream result contract.

Root cause: formatNormalOutput formats the merged filteredOutput under Stdout and always emits the literal Stderr: (empty). This contradicts the advertised separate-stream result contract.

_meta.notes: The shell command is from the issue. The historical reproduction used a scripted model; this case requests the same real tool action through the normal model and does not start a stub server.
